scope: Diagnosis and local engineering repair of the 0.2.53 native Chrome sign-in gate after full Reload; this lane made no browser action, token read, or credential value inspection.
observed: docs/stabilization/runs/admin-signin-001.json records admin@admin.com visible after sign-in and full Reload in the same dev extension ID at 0.2.51, using the prior release artifact.

docs/stabilization/runs/permission-native-retest.json records the same extension ID and path at 0.2.53, then Email — and Sign in to choose across approximately 5, 12, 20, and 30 seconds after Reload. It does not establish that storage was cleared or that refresh failed.

docs/stabilization/reports/permission-native-retest.json additionally records that the later normal Sign in action opened the AI Matrx OAuth route and showed Authorization error (400), Auth session missing! at 06:13:13 UTC. This is a separate sign-in attempt after the false or real signed-out UI; it does not establish the earlier storage state.

docs/stabilization/runs/debugger-build-002.json ties the loaded 0.2.53 development build to source 013fd432147fb3c75185d027e97f233d889dd885. The 0.2.51 artifact came from release-real-005.json and a strict release build.

The checked-in .env.development and .env.production have equal WXT_SUPABASE_URL, WXT_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, and WXT_EXTENSION_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID values; only the URL origin https://db.matrxserver.com and equality booleans were emitted.

The 0.2.53 development bundle contains React development diagnostics ('Expected static flag was missing'); the prior .output/chrome-mv3 release bundle does not. This establishes a material React runtime-mode difference between artifacts.
static_trace: src/hooks/use-auth.ts:26 and :48-58 set a module-wide bootRan=true before the first await, mark that first effect cancelled in cleanup, and skip every later effect setup while bootRan stays true. In a development Strict Mode effect setup/cleanup/setup cycle, the first async hydration is cancelled and the second setup returns; setUser at :61 is never reached.

src/state/auth.ts:15-22 initializes user=null; SettingsView.tsx:127 and :135 display Email — and Sign in to choose from that null user. Thus the exact observed UI follows from skipped hydration even if a session remains in chrome.storage.local.

The auth boot code above is unchanged between 0.2.51 candidate 760c7a1 and 0.2.53 source 013fd43. The only auth-flow source delta in that interval moves Chrome identity calls into src/lib/auth/identity-transport.ts for Safari support; restoreSupabaseSession and refresh logic are unchanged.

src/lib/auth/flow.ts:577-602 restores from persisted local storage; :299-359 only clears storage after refresh decryption failure or a terminal 400/401 for the current refresh ciphertext. A roughly one-hour interval is compatible with a refresh attempt, but no status/log or storage-presence evidence confirms one failed.

ranked_hypotheses.cause: Development React Strict Mode effect replay and the module-wide boot guard suppress auth hydration after Reload.
ranked_hypotheses.prediction: The sign-in gate can coexist with USER_PROFILE and refresh-material keys still present. A focused mount guard that survives effect replay would restore the stored admin without a new OAuth sign-in.
ranked_hypotheses.smallest_proof: Before normal sign-in, in the UI-owned native extension context record only booleans for USER_PROFILE, ACCESS_TOKEN, REFRESH_TOKEN_ENC, REFRESH_TOKEN_IV and the expiry timestamp relative to now; do not output values. If present, run a focused dev-React effect-replay test of useAuth and assert setUser(admin) after storage read.

ranked_hypotheses.cause: A refresh attempt around the token's one-hour lifetime was rejected and clearLocalSession removed the profile and credentials.
ranked_hypotheses.prediction: Those storage keys are absent before a new sign-in and prior worker diagnostics contain a terminal refresh 400/401 or decrypt failure; the UI boot guard is then insufficient to explain missing persisted identity.
ranked_hypotheses.smallest_proof: Inspect only storage-key presence and sanitized refresh status/error category around the reload interval; no token values or raw response bodies.

ranked_hypotheses.cause: The loaded extension uses a different storage namespace or OAuth configuration after build replacement.
ranked_hypotheses.prediction: The extension ID/path or public config fingerprint differs across loaded builds, or the old profile is present under another ID.
ranked_hypotheses.smallest_proof: Already weakened by matching native extension ID/path and equal selected build env values; compare manifest identity and public origin in loaded artifact only if the first two tests do not decide the case.

causal_reproduction.result_before_fix: The same persisted admin fixture hydrated without StrictMode, while two StrictMode cases failed at the user-ID hydration assertion. This isolates effect replay rather than malformed profile, storage, or restore fixture.
causal_reproduction.separate_baseline_issue: The older use-auth-race test mock omitted chrome.storage.session.get after a concurrent Safari auth change. Its two assertions passed but produced two unhandled TypeErrors. The fixture was aligned to the real session API before GREEN verification.

repair.behavior: Count mounted useAuth consumers; invalidate an in-flight boot only when the last consumer unmounts, so development StrictMode replay starts a fresh boot and another mounted consumer can receive hydration. A boot and its later admin lookup must still match the current boot and auth generation before updating state.
guards: src/hooks/use-auth.strict-mode.test.tsx: persisted admin and regular profiles survive StrictMode replay, the positive control hydrates without replay, a remaining consumer hydrates after first-owner unmount, and an old admin lookup cannot restore admin state after sign-out.
tests/unit/use-auth-race.test.tsx: existing overlapping sign-in and cross-consumer sign-out guards retain their assertions with the current Chrome session API mocked.
repair.manual_recipe: docs/feature-tests.md: signed-in identity survives a development build reload

independent_review_and_classification_re.peer_verdict: Engineering FAIL after lifecycle repair: a cached profile appeared signed in when restoreSupabaseSession returned false, and a cached admin flag appeared in guest UI without a profile. The peer explicitly did not claim a backend authorization bypass.
independent_review_and_classification_re.canonical_identity_evidence: src/lib/auth/flow.ts getVerifiedCurrentUser obtains the current or refreshed bearer and verifies its claims locally through verifyBearerClaims; it returns null for invalid or temporarily unverifiable claims without a per-request Auth server user lookup or clearing the saved profile. restoreSupabaseSession alone only installs the token in the Supabase Realtime client and does not verify its identity.
independent_review_and_classification_re.red_receipt: docs/stabilization/runs/auth-classification-red-001.json: five classification assertions failed and eleven existing assertions passed with no unhandled errors before the repair.
independent_review_and_classification_re.repair_behavior: Boot shows signed-in UI only after session restore and a locally verified bearer whose subject matches the cached profile. Missing, unverifiable, or mismatched identity shows guest with a recoverable error while preserving the saved account material. Admin UI waits for the current account's check; a guest cannot access admin tabs from a stale admin flag, and Settings never shows an admin role without a user. A null auth broadcast clears UI admin state.
independent_review_and_classification_re.visible_recovery: src/entrypoints/sidepanel/App.tsx wraps SettingsView in AuthGate; AuthGate displays useAuth error above Settings with a Try again action. The browser recipe in docs/feature-tests.md now covers this recovery state.
independent_review_and_classification_re.verification_state: docs/stabilization/runs/auth-classification-green-001.json records 37 of 37 focused tests passing over seven files with no unhandled errors after commit 553bad3. The fresh peer confirmed the two previous findings addressed and identified three new entrypoint/role-result findings; native reload remains unverified.

round_two_peer_and_pending_design.peer_verdict: Earlier cached-profile/admin findings addressed; three remaining entrypoint findings: incoming auth broadcasts trust their payload before canonical storage validation, interactive sign-in ignores restore false, and an admin lookup error is reported as confirmed non-admin.
caller_census: src/hooks/use-auth.ts boot checks checkIsAdmin after verified hydration; a failed read needs a visible role warning and same-session retry without overwriting the cached admin decision as false.

src/hooks/use-auth.ts interactive sign-in checks checkIsAdmin after OAuth completion; a failed read must keep verified identity while marking role unavailable, rather than claiming non-admin or silently exiting.

src/lib/auth/safari-background.ts checks checkIsAdmin after OAuth completion and broadcasts user/isAdmin; on a failed read it must not broadcast an unverified admin claim, while the receiver must independently rehydrate and show the role warning.

src/lib/supabase/queries.ts checkIsAdmin is the sole role query function; its current error-to-false mapping collapses unavailable and confirmed non-admin. The three callers above are its complete source-call census.
round_two_peer_and_pending_design.planned_shared_boundary: Use one canonical storage rehydration decision for boot, interactive sign-in after committed tokens, and auth broadcasts. The decision awaits restoreSupabaseSession, uses getVerifiedCurrentUser to validate the current bearer, compares the verified subject with any saved/expected profile, and reports a recoverable guest state without deleting credentials when unavailable. Broadcast payloads only trigger this decision and never supply the displayed identity or admin role. A generation check prevents an older async decision from overwriting a newer sign-out or sign-in.
round_two_peer_and_pending_design.planned_role_result: Let checkIsAdmin return true, false, or null for read failure, update all three callers, and keep the UI admin flag false until confirmed true. Null shows a role-check warning with a retry action that rechecks the current session rather than starting OAuth; the query error never writes a false cache value.
round_two_peer_and_pending_design.state: Design only. Root coordinator controls the queued RED run and no round-two production edit has been made.
